intro: You are about to walk through the whole of Anatolia's past in a single building: the Museum of Anatolian Civilizations, in Ankara province, founded in 1921. Housed in an Ottoman bedesten, it tells Anatolia's story from the Palaeolithic to Rome along a single route, and it holds the world's fullest Hittite and Neo-Hittite collection.
history: The museum was created by restoring and joining two old buildings: the fifteenth-century Mahmut Pasha bedesten and the Kurşunlu Han. It began with Atatürk's wish for a 'Hittite Museum', and grew into a collection covering every period of Anatolia. The display is chronological: you start in the Palaeolithic and walk on through the Çatalhöyük, Hittite, Phrygian and Urartian halls, all the way to Rome.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Çatalhöyük hall and the Hittite hall, then the Neo-Hittite orthostats, and further on the Phrygian hall and the Urartian hall.
facts: Did you know? In 1997 it was named European Museum of the Year — the first museum in Türkiye to win the award. The museum was made by restoring and joining a fifteenth-century bedesten and a han, so the building itself is part of the collection. And it holds the world's fullest Hittite and Neo-Hittite collection: the orthostats of Karatepe, Carchemish and Arslantepe line up together in one hall.
outro: This brings our journey through the Museum of Anatolian Civilizations to an end. Please leave the objects untouched and take your photographs without flash. These pieces have survived through every age of Anatolia; let them keep their story for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
